mbm-1851.clue: I need a smaller pencil for Sundays.
mbm-1851.quote: My ham-radio log has a tiny space for weather. One operator reported a single cloud shaped like a teapot, so I drew it. The next Sunday four people called in with new shapes.

mbm-1852.clue: Save the little purple mitten for the tree.
mbm-1852.quote: I spotted my lost mitten high in a pine from the chairlift. It spent the rest of the winter up there, waving at us every run. I made it the landmark on our family trail map.

mbm-1853.clue: I hold the postcard by the wings.
mbm-1853.quote: My collection of airplane postcards has worn spots where my thumbs make the turns. I take the closest match to the airfield and let the real plane teach the paper one its approach.

mbm-1854.clue: The best part of my kayak is the scratch you can see.
mbm-1854.quote: I scraped a little paint off the bow on my first river trip. My sister added an eye behind the mark in waterproof paint. Now I paddle a green crocodile with a chipped smile.

mbm-1855.clue: I like climbing when the shadows have long fingers.
mbm-1855.quote: At sunset the shadow of my hand reaches the final hold before I do. For a week I practiced getting there at the same time. When I managed it, I gave my shadow a very small high five.

mbm-1856.clue: We hang our sunglasses on the winner's end.
mbm-1856.quote: We borrowed the fishing net stakes for beach volleyball and kept forgetting which side was ahead. A row of bright glasses on the post does the job now. The gulls have yet to join a team.

mbm-1857.clue: I paint what happens at the edges.
mbm-1857.quote: At the winter market I painted mittened hands passing a cup over the edge of my canvas. The stall owner asked where the faces were. Then she recognized her own patched mitten and bought me cocoa.

mbm-1858.clue: The green strip has a catch in it.
mbm-1858.quote: I quilted the pattern of our old back gate, complete with a little brass hook sewn to the cloth. My mother instinctively lifts the hook when she unfolds the blanket.

mbm-1859.clue: I draw the greens with my eyes shut first.
mbm-1859.quote: Before a putt I trace the slope with my finger on my scorecard. My uncle traced one so crooked we thought he'd lost his nerve. The ball followed it like a train.

mbm-1860.clue: You can hear my first gig in a biscuit tin.
mbm-1860.quote: Our drummer was late for rehearsal, so I tapped the rhythm on Gran's empty tin. We kept it for the quiet verse at the show. She wants her royalties paid in biscuits.

mbm-1861.clue: My flight log includes a terrier.
mbm-1861.quote: I sketch the little planes at our airfield, then draw whoever's waiting by the hangar. One terrier has attended more landings than any of the humans. He gets a whole page.

mbm-1862.clue: I put a loose button down where the divot was.
mbm-1862.quote: My first outing with Dad I kept overthinking the short putts. He laid his spare jacket button on the grass and asked me to get near it. That's still the smallest target I've ever hit.

mbm-1863.clue: I saved the piece with the faded apples.
mbm-1863.quote: I made a quilt from the old canvas fruit sacks in Grandpa's shed. The red apple stamp on one sack just fits in the middle. Grandpa took one look and named the orchard.

mbm-1864.clue: I keep a spoon tied to the rear rack.
mbm-1864.quote: When the cycle route crosses the canal, we stop by the woman who sells strawberry cups. I brought a real spoon once. It jingled all the way home and has lived on the bike since.

mbm-1865.clue: I can tell that aircraft by its shoe.
mbm-1865.quote: At the aerodrome open day I drew only landing wheels, one to a page. An old pilot matched every one to its plane. He missed his own until I showed him the scuff on the rim.

mbm-1866.clue: The quietest page is the loudest one at home.
mbm-1866.quote: Dad read our favorite book aloud until the page with the missing corner, then made up his own ending. I found a whole copy last week. I'm keeping Dad's ending.

mbm-1867.clue: My rain jacket has a slice of cake in the pocket.
mbm-1867.quote: I sewed on a cake-shaped patch for every bicycle ride that ended at a bakery. The pocket is full now. My riding partner says the sleeves have miles of room.

mbm-1868.clue: Nobody arrives late to our tower on Tuesdays.
mbm-1868.quote: I rang one bell for the first time while my sister stood outside the tower and drew a line for each sound. She showed me the notebook afterward. I can see exactly when I found the rhythm.

mbm-1869.clue: The best hole has no number.
mbm-1869.quote: The mini golf owner let us draw a course on the concrete while the windmill was being repaired. My cousin drew a spiral around a leaf. We took turns till the leaf blew away.

mbm-1870.clue: I leave the ribbon tied in my suitcase.
mbm-1870.quote: I make two silk scarves change places, red in my hand and yellow in a box. Dad tied them together before the first show in case I got lonely. I keep that knot for the trip home.

mbm-1871.clue: I count dominoes in planting season.
mbm-1871.quote: We marked our vegetable rows with extra dominoes when the little signs blew away. Two dots for beans, three for carrots. A neighbor came to play, saw the garden and said I'd got a very promising hand.

mbm-1872.clue: We've got a rule for tiny spectators.
mbm-1872.quote: When my nephew watches, he parks a toy bus by the board. Any piece sent home gets a ride. Losing is less painful when the driver announces the stops.

mbm-1873.clue: I learned to fold the uniform before I learned the form.
mbm-1873.quote: My instructor taught our class to smooth the sleeves and line up the edges at the end of practice. Mine went home in a heap for months. Now my youngest cousin asks me to fold hers.

mbm-1874.clue: I sing in the loudest socks I own.
mbm-1874.quote: My duet partner gets butterflies before we go on. Last time she held up her striped pair while I pulled mine on. By the time we settled whether stripes clash with diamonds, she'd already sung the opening note.

mbm-1875.clue: The cartoon dog has to wait for the bus.
mbm-1875.quote: Our anime club sketched a little dog on the clear sheets from an old overhead projector. We walked the sheets past a drawing of a bus stop. When the dog finally sat down, everybody clapped.
